items.title: Characteristic function of a real random variable
items.statement: For a real random variable X, define phi_X(t)=E exp(itX)=integral exp(itx) P_X(dx), t real. Complex expectation means the componentwise real integral. The same notation applies to a specified Borel probability law.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Composition with sine and cosine is measurable; their absolute values are bounded by one on a probability space. Apply the complex change-of-variables theorem; no moment assumption is needed.

items.title: Basic properties of characteristic functions
items.statement: Every characteristic function satisfies phi(0)=1, |phi(t)|<=1, phi(-t)=conjugate(phi(t)), and is uniformly continuous on R.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Bound |phi(t+h)-phi(t)| by E|exp(ihX)-1|, independent of t. This tends to zero by DCT with bound 2. Unit mass gives the value at zero; the integral triangle inequality gives the modulus bound and componentwise integration gives conjugation.

items.title: Characteristic functions under affine maps and independent sums
items.statement: For real a,b, phi_(aX+b)(t)=exp(itb)phi_X(at). For any finite mutually independent family of real random variables, phi_(sum X_j)=product phi_X_j; the empty sum has characteristic function 1.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Use the exponential addition law. Expand the finite product of cos(tX_j)+i sin(tX_j) into real products and apply the published real bounded-factor independence theorem to each product, then recombine. No finite-range assumption and no existence of moments is used.

items.title: Positive definite function on the real line
items.statement: A complex function psi on R is positive definite if for all n>=1, real t_j and complex z_j, sum_(j,k) z_j conjugate(z_k) psi(t_j-t_k) is real and nonnegative. This definition asserts no representation theorem.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.title: Characteristic functions are positive definite
items.statement: Every characteristic function is positive definite.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: The displayed quadratic form equals E|sum_j z_j exp(it_j X)|^2. The finite sum is bounded, so all expectations exist. Expand the square and use linearity.

items.title: Characteristic function fourier stieltjes convention
items.statement: Under the FA convention hat(mu)(xi)=integral exp(-2 pi i x xi)mu(dx), phi_X(t)=hat(P_X)(-t/(2 pi)). No change of normalization or sign is implicit.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Substitute xi=-t/(2 pi). The required FA supplier is planned only and absent on disk; this interface remains blocked.

items.title: Uniqueness of a law from its characteristic function
items.statement: Assume AC for the planned FA uniqueness route. Two Borel probability laws on R with the same characteristic function are equal.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: After substituting -t/(2 pi), apply FA finite-Borel-measure uniqueness. AC is propagated provisionally from the planned regularity/smoothing route; the exact supplier proof and axiom closure must be reviewed when published. Do not replace it by citing this page's later inversion theorem. As an inline consequence, a real-valued characteristic function gives phi_(-X)=conjugate(phi_X)=phi_X, hence X and -X have the same law; conversely symmetry gives reality.

items.title: Uniform sine integral bound and dirichlet value
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited Riemann/Lebesgue bridge. S(T)=integral_0^T sin(u)/u du (value 1 at zero) is uniformly bounded for T>=0 and tends to pi/2. Consequently integral_-T^T sin(tz)/t dt tends to pi sign(z), uniformly bounded in T,z.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: On [1,T] integration by parts bounds the tail from A by 3/A, uniformly also for e^(-epsilon u)/u since that multiplier decreases; compact integrals handle zero. For epsilon>0 use sin(u)/u=integral_0^1 cos(su)ds and absolute Fubini (bound integral e^(-epsilon u)du finite). The elementary Laplace cosine integral is epsilon/(epsilon^2+s^2), evaluated by the primitive e^(-epsilon u)(-epsilon cos(su)+s sin(su))/(epsilon^2+s^2). Integration in s gives arctan(1/epsilon). Uniform tail bounds and compact DCT identify its epsilon-downarrow-zero limit with S(infinity)=pi/2. Scaling and oddness give the final assertion. The compact integral bridge consumes countable choice, supplied by AC; no absolute integrability of sin(u)/u on the whole half-line is asserted.

items.title: Levy inversion formula
items.statement: Assume AC for the analytic integration bridge. For a<b, the symmetric truncations (2 pi)^(-1) integral_-T^T [(exp(-ita)-exp(-itb))/(it)] phi_X(t)dt converge to P(a<X<b)+(P(X=a)+P(X=b))/2. In particular they recover the open-interval mass when endpoints have no atoms. At t=0 the quotient means b-a.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: The quotient equals integral_a^b exp(-ity)dy and is bounded by b-a. Fubini on the finite t interval and the probability measure is legitimate. The resulting inner integral is R_T(x-a)-R_T(x-b), with R_T(z)=integral_-T^T sin(tz)/t dt. Apply the uniform bound and limit in the preceding lemma, then DCT in x. The limiting sign difference is 2 pi in the interior, pi at either endpoint, and zero outside.

items.title: Density inversion from an integrable characteristic function
items.statement: Assume AC as in Levy inversion. If phi_X is Lebesgue integrable, its law has the bounded continuous density f(x)=(2 pi)^(-1) integral_R exp(-itx)phi_X(t)dt.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: DCT gives continuity, conjugate symmetry gives reality, and |f|<=(2 pi)^(-1)||phi||_1. Inversion bounds every interval and its half endpoint masses by its length times this constant; shrinking intervals shows there are no atoms. Absolute Fubini gives mu((a,b))=integral_a^b f. If f were negative at any point continuity would contradict positive interval mass. The measure f dx has total one by increasing intervals; finite-measure uniqueness extends interval equality to all Borel sets.

items.title: Moments give derivatives of the characteristic function
items.statement: If k is a nonnegative integer and E|X|^k<infinity, then phi_X is C^k and phi_X^(j)(t)=E[(iX)^j exp(itX)] for 0<=j<=k.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: All lower powers are integrable since |x|^j<=1+|x|^k. The difference quotient of exp(itx) is bounded by |x|, using its integral along the real parameter segment. At stage j the bound is |x|^j. DCT gives each derivative inductively; a second DCT with the same bound gives its continuity.

items.title: A prescribed finite jet at zero does not determine the law
items.statement: The moment-to-derivative theorem is one-directional. No converse or moment-determinacy theorem is asserted; finitely many moments never suffice in general.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: The B companion gives a finite witness for any prescribed finite number of moments; it is explanatory, not a proof dependency. Do not infer that the full derivative sequence determines a law.

items.title: Levy continuity theorem forward direction
items.statement: If Borel probability laws mu_n converge weakly to mu on R, then their characteristic functions converge at every real t.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: For each fixed t test weak convergence with the bounded continuous real functions cos(tx) and sin(tx) and combine their limits.

items.title: Tightness from characteristic function equicontinuity at zero
items.statement: Assume AC for the compact-interval integration bridge. A family of Borel probability laws whose characteristic functions are equicontinuous at zero is tight. More precisely for delta>0 and w_delta(t)=(1-|t|/delta)_+/delta, mu(|x|>=4/delta)<=(4/3) integral w_delta(t)(1-Re phi_mu(t))dt.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Compute integral w_delta(t)cos(tx)dt=[sin(delta x/2)/(delta x/2)]^2, continuously 1 at x=0, by two elementary integrations. This quantity lies in [0,1], and is <=1/4 if |x|>=4/delta. Thus integrating 1 minus this quantity against mu bounds (3/4) times its tail. Fubini applies to bounded integrands on a finite parameter interval. The weight has mass one. Equicontinuity makes the right side uniformly small; [-4/delta,4/delta] is compact.

items.title: Levy continuity theorem converse
items.statement: Assume AC. If phi_n(t) converges pointwise to psi(t) and psi is continuous at zero, there is a unique Borel probability law mu with characteristic function psi, and mu_n converges weakly to mu.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Do not assume pointwise convergence gives equicontinuity. For a fixed delta, DCT transfers the triangular-weight integral in the preceding tail bound to psi. Since psi(0)=1 and psi is continuous at zero, choose delta with small limiting integral, then control all sufficiently late n. Enlarge the compact interval to cover the finitely many earlier laws, using continuity from below. This proves tightness directly with the lemma's quantitative bound. Prokhorov extracts a weak limit; the forward theorem identifies its characteristic function with psi; FA uniqueness identifies every extracted limit. A failing bounded continuous test would give a subsequence separated from the claimed limit and contradict the same extraction. AC covers Prokhorov and its countable compact choices.

items.title: Characteristic function criterion for weak convergence
items.statement: Assume AC. For a specified Borel probability law mu, mu_n converges weakly to mu iff phi_n(t) converges to phi_mu(t) for every t.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: The forward direction uses bounded continuous tests. For the reverse the target characteristic function is continuous at zero by the basic lemma, so the converse theorem applies.

items.title: Cramer wold device
items.statement: Assume AC. Borel probability laws on R^d are determined by the laws of every real linear projection. If for each theta in R^d the theta-projections of mu_n converge weakly to that of a fixed law mu, then mu_n converges weakly to mu.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Define Phi_mu(t)=integral exp(i t dot x)mu(dx); this equals the one-dimensional characteristic function of t dot X at 1. Equality of all projections gives equality of the d-dimensional Fourier transforms and hence equality of laws by the planned FA theorem in dimension d. For convergence, the d coordinate projections are tight; a union bound outside a product of d compact intervals gives tightness on R^d. Prokhorov and the continuous-mapping theorem show every subsequential law has all the projections of mu; d-dimensional uniqueness identifies it. The bounded-test subsequence argument closes convergence. A one-dimensional uniqueness theorem alone is inadequate.

title: Characteristic Functions Inversion and Continuity — Examples

items.title: Characteristic functions of bernoulli binomial and poisson laws
items.statement: For Bernoulli(p), Binomial(n,p) and Poisson(lambda) laws the characteristic functions are 1-p+p exp(it), (1-p+p exp(it))^n and exp(lambda(exp(it)-1)), including p=0,1, n=0 and lambda=0.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Define the three laws by their masses. The binomial theorem sums the finite masses and transform. The exponential series normalizes e^(-lambda)lambda^k/k! and sums its transform absolutely, since the absolute terms sum to one. No Poisson process is constructed. For finite mixtures sum_j a_j mu_j, linearity gives phi=sum_j a_j phi_j whenever a_j>=0 and sum_j a_j=1.

items.title: Characteristic function of the uniform law
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. For the uniform law on [a,b], a<b, phi(t)=(exp(itb)-exp(ita))/(it(b-a)) for t nonzero, and phi(0)=1.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Normalize the interval-indicator density. Integrate real and imaginary parts over [a,b] using their primitives and the compact integral bridge. The continuous extension at zero follows either from the integral formula or the basic bounded convergence argument. AC supplies countable choice for the bridge.

items.title: Characteristic function of a gaussian law
items.statement: Assume AC for the integration bridge. N(m,sigma^2) has characteristic function exp(imt-sigma^2 t^2/2), also for sigma=0 as the Dirac law at m.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: For the standard density g, |x|g is integrable by the primitive of exp(-x^2/2). DCT differentiates phi. Since g'= -xg, integration by parts on [-R,R] with vanishing Gaussian boundary gives phi'=-t phi. The derivative of exp(t^2/2)phi is zero; phi(0)=1 gives the result. Apply affine scaling; handle sigma=0 directly. No imaginary shift or contour integral is used.

items.title: Cauchy law and its characteristic function
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. The density 1/[pi(1+x^2)] has characteristic function exp(-|t|) and has no finite first absolute moment.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: First normalize the auxiliary Laplace density exp(-|x|)/2, and compute its characteristic function 1/(1+t^2) by elementary exponential integration on each half-line. It is integrable (arctangent primitive). Apply density inversion to that known law: its continuous density equals (2 pi)^(-1) integral exp(-itx)/(1+t^2)dt everywhere, since two continuous representatives agreeing almost everywhere agree everywhere. Relabel variables to obtain the claimed Cauchy transform. The arctangent primitive normalizes the Cauchy density; integral_0^R x/(pi(1+x^2))dx=log(1+R^2)/(2 pi) diverges. Neither first-moment existence nor a contour integral is assumed. The half-line computation also gives the one-sided unit exponential transform 1/(1-it), before averaging its reflected law.

items.title: Independent sums via characteristic functions
items.statement: Assume AC. If X_j are independent Bernoulli(p), their sum has Binomial(n,p) law. Independent Poisson(lambda), Poisson(eta) variables sum to Poisson(lambda+eta). A finite sum of independent normal variables is normal with the sums of their means and variances.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Sum the Bernoulli masses to obtain 1-p+p exp(it), use the binomial theorem for the Binomial law, and sum the absolutely convergent Poisson exponential series to obtain exp(lambda(exp(it)-1)). Multiply these transforms and invoke A-page uniqueness. For independent normal inputs, locally derive the standard normal transform by differentiating under its integral and integrating by parts to obtain phi prime=-t phi, phi(0)=1; affine scaling gives exp(imt-sigma^2 t^2/2). Multiplication adds means and variances, so the sum is normal, including deterministic zero-variance cases. All hypotheses of Gaussian normalization, compact integration by parts and DCT match the displayed densities; Gaussian boundary terms vanish. No B item is a supplier.

items.title: Density inversion for a triangular characteristic function
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. The triangular characteristic function (1-|t|)_+ corresponds to the probability density (1-cos x)/(pi x^2), with value 1/(2 pi) at zero.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Start with the known probability density h(u)=(1-|u|)_+. Two integrations give its characteristic function q(s)=2(1-cos s)/s^2, continuous value 1 at zero; q is nonnegative and integrable by a bounded-near-zero and 4/s^2 tail bound. Apply inversion to h: h(y)=(2 pi)^(-1) integral exp(-isy)q(s)ds. At y=0 this proves integral q=2 pi, so q/(2 pi) is a probability density. Relabel s=x,y=-t to identify its transform as h(t). This first establishes that the triangle is a characteristic function, avoiding circular use of density inversion.

items.title: Pointwise limit discontinuous at zero signals mass escape
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. The uniform laws on [-n,n] have characteristic functions sin(nt)/(nt), value 1 at zero; their pointwise limit is 1 at zero and 0 elsewhere and is not a characteristic function.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Integrate exp(itx)/(2n) on [-n,n] componentwise, using the sine/cosine primitives and the compact Riemann/Lebesgue bridge; this gives sin(nt)/(nt), with value one at zero. At fixed nonzero t use |sin(nt)/(nt)|<=1/(n|t|). Each fixed interval [-M,M] has mass min(1,M/n), tending to zero, so the family is not tight. The discontinuous limit contradicts the continuity of every characteristic function.

items.title: Equal finitely many moments do not determine a law
items.statement: For every integer m>=0 there are distinct finitely supported probability laws with equal moments of orders 0 through m.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Norris, Probability and Measure

items.strategy: Put N=m+1. Give the even k in {0,...,N} masses binomial(N,k)/2^(N-1) and the odd k the same respective masses in the other law. Their total masses equal one by (1+1)^N and (1-1)^N. The Nth finite difference of each polynomial k^j with j<N is zero: one difference lowers degree by one, so induction proves sum(-1)^k binomial(N,k)k^j=0. Supports are disjoint, so the laws differ. For m=2 this gives even masses (1/4 at 0,3/4 at 2) versus (3/4 at 1,1/4 at 3).

title: Conditional Distributions and Regular Conditional Probability

items.title: Measure kernel and probability kernel
items.statement: A measure kernel K from (S,Sigma) to (T,Tau) assigns a measure K(s,.) to every s and has measurable evaluations s->K(s,A). It is a probability kernel if K(s,T)=1 everywhere. A finite kernel has finite mass at each s; a uniformly sigma-finite kernel has a specified measurable exhaustion T_n increasing to T with K(s,T_n)<infinity for every s,n. No common bound in s is required. A general measure kernel need not have such an exhaustion.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.title: Measurability of integration against a kernel
items.statement: For a probability or finite kernel K, and a nonnegative Sigma tensor Tau measurable f(s,t), s->integral f(s,t)K(s,dt) is measurable. The same holds for a uniformly sigma-finite kernel with the specified exhaustion. For real f the signed integral is measurable on {integral |f| K<infinity}, and extending by 0 outside that measurable set gives a measurable real function.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: For finite K, the class of product sets A whose section evaluation K(s,A_s) is measurable contains rectangles. It is a lambda-system: subtract from the finite measurable mass K(s,T) for complements and use countable nonnegative sums for disjoint unions. Pi-lambda yields all product-measurable indicators, then simple approximation and sectionwise MCT give f. For uniformly sigma-finite K apply the finite result to K(s,. intersect T_n), then MCT. Signed integrals are differences of the two nonnegative integrals only on the finite absolute-integral set. An unrestricted measure-kernel claim has not been justified and is owner-escalated; all consumers use the proved probability case.

items.title: Composition of probability kernels
items.statement: For probability kernels K:S->T and L:T->U, write (KL)(s,A)=integral L(t,A)K(s,dt), with the resulting probability-kernel assertion proved in the following lemma.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.title: Kernel composition is well defined and associative
items.statement: Composition of probability kernels is a probability kernel, and (KL)M=K(LM) pointwise for specified kernels.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Measurability of L(.,A) and the integration theorem give measurable evaluations. Sectionwise MCT proves countable additivity and integration of 1 gives total mass one. Establish integral h(u)(KL)(s,du)=integral K(s,dt) integral h(u)L(t,du) first for indicators by definition, then simple functions and increasing limits. Apply this identity to h(u)=M(u,A) to prove associativity. Ordinary product-measure Tonelli alone does not apply to a varying kernel; the preceding monotone argument supplies the needed iterated-kernel identity.

items.title: Conditional probability given a sigma algebra
items.statement: Assume AC for existence. For A in F and G a sub-sigma-algebra, P(A|G) denotes the conditional-expectation class E[1_A|G], not a canonical pointwise probability measure.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.title: Regular conditional distribution
items.statement: For X:Omega->T measurable and G subset F, a regular conditional distribution is a probability kernel K:(Omega,G)->T such that integral_H K(omega,A)P(domega)=P(H intersect {X in A}) for every H in G and A in Tau. Equivalently each evaluation is a conditional-probability version; no common exceptional set is asserted by separately choosing versions.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.title: Regular conditional probability
items.statement: On a standard-Borel sample measurable space (Omega,F), a regular conditional probability given a sub-sigma-algebra G is a regular conditional distribution of the identity map. This definition makes no existence claim on an arbitrary sample measurable space.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.title: Simultaneous rational conditional distribution function versions
items.statement: Assume AC. For real X and any G subset F, there exist simultaneous rational conditional-CDF versions with the stated bounds, order, tails and right limits. The proof locally supplies the zero-complement simple-integral repair, separate zero-scalar rule, nonnegative MCT, bounded decreasing convergence and finite positive RN/conditional-density interface used by this batch.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: First adjoin zero-coefficient complements to arbitrary simple displays and refine them, proving representation independence. Derive nonnegative additivity, positive-scalar homogeneity with a separate zero case, MCT and bounded decreasing convergence. Prove the finite positive RN construction directly by the maximal-density/Hahn argument, then derive uniqueness, order, constants and monotone event limits. Apply this repaired conditional-density interface to rational cuts, unite the countable failures and fill by the delta_0 CDF. Establish measurability of the increasing supremum before applying monotone convergence.

items.title: Rational conditional distribution functions produce real regular kernels
items.statement: Assume AC. Such rational conditional CDF data produce a real regular conditional probability kernel, everywhere a probability measure, with F_omega(x)=inf_(q rational,q>x)G_q(omega) off the exceptional set and delta_0 on it.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Build the right-continuous CDF from rational data. Use only the existence clause of Stieltjes correspondence, then prove uniqueness locally from the closed-half-line generating pi-system and finite-measure pi-lambda. The repaired preceding integral interface supplies bounded decreasing convergence for cut identities and MCT for the final lambda-system extension. Use rational density and a fixed enumeration to construct the required decreasing rational approximants explicitly.

items.title: Existence of regular conditional distributions for standard borel targets
items.statement: Assume AC. Every random element in a standard-Borel target has an everywhere probability regular conditional distribution given any sub-sigma-algebra. For its nonempty target the construction also supplies a bimeasurable real coding and a countable generating, separating and finite-measure-determining algebra.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: From a Polish presentation, embed by distances to an enumerated dense set and prove injectivity plus the inverse-continuity estimate. Prove directly that the weighted cube metric induces the product topology and is complete; the image is therefore G_delta, and the existing explicit cube code restricts to a Borel real code. Pull back rational cuts, form finite Boolean algebras and use finite-measure pi-lambda for the countable determining algebra. Then code X, apply the repaired real kernel and fill the null support-failure fibres by a Dirac mass.

items.title: Simultaneous ae uniqueness of regular conditional distributions
items.statement: Assume AC for the countable determining-algebra supplier. Two regular conditional distributions of the same standard-Borel-valued X given G agree as measures outside one G-measurable null set.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Use the countable determining algebra supplied by the repaired in-batch existence theorem. For each algebra event, prove scalar version uniqueness directly from nonnegative integral monotonicity and additivity on the measurable level sets {u>=v+1/m}; unite the countably many null discrepancies and apply measure determination.

items.title: Conditional integration through a regular conditional law
items.statement: For a specified regular conditional law K of X given G, and nonnegative measurable f, integral f(x)K(omega,dx) satisfies the defining nonnegative conditional event identities. Under AC it represents E[f(X)|G]. If E|f(X)|<infinity, its signed integral is finite almost surely and, after zero extension on the measurable exceptional set, represents the real conditional expectation.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Start with target indicators using the kernel definition, then finite nonnegative sums, then increasing simple approximation and ordinary MCT for every G-event. Apply the result to |f| to see that the kernel absolute integral has expectation E|f(X)|, so is finite almost surely. Positive and negative parts now give the signed claim without infinity-infinity. AC is only for the inherited CE class notation/existence, not for the event-identity argument with a specified kernel.

items.title: Conditional law given a random element
items.statement: A conditional law of X given Y is a probability kernel K from the value space of Y to that of X such that K(Y(omega),A) is a conditional version for each A. Its equivalence class is determined only P_Y-almost everywhere under a countable determining-class hypothesis; values on null fibres can differ.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.title: Regular conditional kernels factor through a standard borel conditioning variable
items.statement: Assume AC. If E,T are nonempty standard-Borel spaces and L is a regular conditional distribution of E-valued X given sigma(Y), Y valued in T, there is a probability kernel K:T->E with L(omega,.)=K(Y(omega),.) simultaneously outside a single null set.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Use the real coding supplied by the repaired in-batch existence theorem. Supply bounded scalar factorization by AC-selected dyadic-bin lifts. Construct the real kernel from rational CDF data using only CDF existence, prove CDF uniqueness locally by closed-half-line pi-lambda, establish evaluation measurability by pointwise limits, repair support and pull back.

items.title: Disintegration of a joint law on standard borel spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. For a joint probability law of (X,Y) on standard-Borel E times T there exists a probability kernel K:T->E such that P_(X,Y)(A times B)=integral_B K(y,A)P_Y(dy). It is unique as a kernel P_Y-almost everywhere, and the corresponding iterated identity holds for all nonnegative joint-measurable tests.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Obtain and factor the coordinate RCD using the repaired in-batch interfaces. Prove marginal substitution first for indicators, then simple functions and local MCT. Prove kernel-integral measurability by a product-event lambda-system, the indicator identity by a second lambda-system, and extend by prescribed simple approximants and local MCT. Transport simultaneous uniqueness through Y and use the in-batch determining algebra to obtain one measurable marginal-null discrepancy set. Establish section measurability and kernel-evaluation measurability together by a lambda-system argument.

items.title: Conditional expectation as a measurable function of the conditioning variable
items.statement: Assume AC. In the preceding standard-Borel setting, E[f(X)|sigma(Y)]=h(Y) almost surely where h(y)=integral f(x)K(y,dx), for nonnegative or integrable f, with zero filling on exceptional signed-integrability fibres.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Measurability of h follows from kernel integration. Substitution into the RCD conditional-integration formula proves the identity. For integrable f, the nonnegative identity for |f| makes bad fibres P_Y-null. The statement is an almost-sure identity, not a canonical value at every y.

items.title: Conditional density formula
items.statement: Let a joint law on E times T have nonnegative product-measurable density p(x,y) relative to sigma-finite measures mu times nu. Put m(y)=integral p(x,y)mu(dx). On 0<m(y)<infinity define K(y,A)=integral_A p(x,y)mu(dx)/m(y); on all other fibres use a specified fixed probability rho on E. Then K is a probability kernel and satisfies the conditional-law rectangle identity. If CE class notation is used assume AC. Infinite marginal-density fibres, as well as zero fibres, require filling.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Tonelli proves m measurable and integral m dnu=1, so {m=infinity} is nu-null and hence marginal-null after choosing a finite-a.e. density version. The set {m=0} also has zero marginal mass. Section integrals over A are measurable. On the good set their normalization is a probability; the measurable fixed filler makes all other fibres probabilities. Tonelli on each rectangle recovers the joint probability; exceptional fibres contribute zero. Do not assert finite positive normalizer at every point merely from integrability of the joint density.

items.title: Bayes formula for dominated kernels
items.statement: Given a prior probability pi on E and a dominated likelihood kernel with nonnegative jointly measurable density ell(theta,y) relative to a sigma-finite observation measure nu, define m(y)=integral ell(theta,y)pi(dtheta). On 0<m<infinity the posterior is K(y,A)=integral_A ell(theta,y)pi(dtheta)/m(y), filled with pi where m=0 or infinity. It is a conditional law of the parameter given the observation.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: The nonnegative joint density ell relative to pi times nu has integral one because every likelihood section has nu integral one. Apply the conditional density theorem with parameter as x and observation as y. The prior itself is a fixed measurable filler. Infinite-normalizer fibres are marginal-null and cannot be normalized by a formal infinity/infinity ratio.

title: Conditional Distributions and Regular Conditional Probability — Examples

items.title: Regular conditional law for a finite partition
items.statement: For a finite measurable partition H_1,...,H_n, the conditional law of X on each positive-mass cell H_j is P(X in A,H_j)/P(H_j); zero-mass cells receive one fixed target probability.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Every evaluation is constant on partition cells and hence measurable. Positive cells give probability measures by restriction and normalization; the chosen filler covers zero cells. Any event in the generated sigma-algebra is a union of cells, so summing the defining identities verifies the RCD property.

items.title: Conditional density of a bivariate normal law
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. For sigma_X,sigma_Y>0 and |r|<1, the usual bivariate normal density with means m_X,m_Y, standard deviations sigma_X,sigma_Y and correlation r yields X|Y=y distributed as N(m_X+r sigma_X(y-m_Y)/sigma_Y, sigma_X^2(1-r^2)).

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Specify the joint density as exp(-(u^2-2ruv+v^2)/(2(1-r^2)))/(2 pi sigma_X sigma_Y sqrt(1-r^2)), where u,v are standardized coordinates. Complete u^2-2ruv+v^2=(u-rv)^2+(1-r^2)v^2. The Gaussian normalization gives the marginal normal density and total mass one. Divide by its everywhere positive value. For singular |r|=1 no joint Lebesgue density exists; that case is outside the density hypothesis, not an implicit zero-variance quotient.

items.title: Conditioning independent variables leaves the marginal law
items.statement: For independent random elements X,Y, the constant probability kernel K(y,A)=P_X(A) is a conditional law of X given Y.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Constant evaluations are measurable. Independence gives P(X in A,Y in B)=P_X(A)P_Y(B); integrate the constant kernel to verify every rectangle. This works without a standard-Borel existence theorem because the kernel is explicit.

items.title: Bayes formula for a finite mixture with continuous observation
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. Let J take values 0,1 with probabilities p,1-p, 0<p<1, and let Y|J=j have normal density g_j with means j and variance 1. The posterior probability of J=1 is (1-p)g_1(y)/(p g_0(y)+(1-p)g_1(y)).

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Construct the joint distribution from the two weighted densities on {0,1} times R. Its total mass is one and marginal density is positive everywhere. Apply the displayed Bayes normalization; at y=1/2 the two likelihoods agree and the posterior equals 1-p. No empirical/statistical interpretation is used as proof.

items.title: Regular conditional law of one coordinate given another
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. Under the uniform probability density 2 on {(x,y):0<x<y<1}, the first coordinate conditioned on Y=y is uniform on (0,y) for 0<y<1, with fixed delta_0 filler elsewhere.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Integrate in x to get marginal m(y)=2y on (0,1), whose integral is one. The ratio is 1/y on (0,y). For rectangles integrate (1/y) length(A intersect (0,y)) against 2y dy; this equals the joint probability. No ratio is evaluated at y=0.

items.title: A deterministic kernel from a measurable map
items.statement: A measurable map g:S->T defines the deterministic probability kernel K(s,A)=1_A(g(s)); composing two such kernels gives the kernel of the composite map.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: For each s the section is the Dirac measure at g(s), and every evaluation is the indicator of a measurable preimage. Integration against that Dirac measure yields the claimed composition, including on null fibres.

items.title: The density ratio is undefined on zero marginal fibres
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. For the uniform density on the square (0,1)^2, the density ratio for X given Y=y is 0/0 at y=2. The constant uniform-on-(0,1) kernel is a valid measurable extension.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: The marginal is 1_(0,1)(y), and the density section at 2 vanishes identically. Division is undefined. The constant uniform kernel agrees with the ratio on the positive-marginal set; integration against P_Y ignores the complement, proving the conditional rectangle identity.

items.title: Regular conditional laws are not unique on null conditioning values
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited integration/existence suppliers. Let Y be uniform on (0,1) and X=0 identically, with real target. Kernels delta_0 everywhere and delta_1 at y=1/2 but delta_0 elsewhere are distinct versions of the same conditional law.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition
Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4

items.strategy: Singleton {1/2} is Borel and P_Y-null. The modified evaluation equals 1_A(0)+1_{1/2}(y)(1_A(1)-1_A(0)), hence is measurable, and every section is a probability. Both rectangle integrals equal 1_A(0)P_Y(B), but their measures at y=1/2 differ.
